newsitem.title: OMAN: Gulf Arabs told they face bleak water future.
newsitem.headline: Gulf Arabs told they face bleak water future.

text.p: Gulf Arab states could face acute water shortage within a century unless serious water policies are adopted to rationlise consumption and find cheaper desalination technology, water experts said on Sunday.
"Water reserves in the Gulf Cooperation Coucil (GCC) states will only last for one century," said Mohammad Abdul-Karim al-Soufi, head of the Bahrain-based Water Sciences and Technology Association.
Soufi who was addressing the third Gulf Water Technology Conference in Muscat, said GCC states had to find cheaper water desalination methods and rationlaise consumption.
The GCC, a political and economic alliance, groups Saudi Arabia, Oman, Kuwait, Bahrain, Qatar and the United Arab Emirates.
"Ground water reserves for irrigation will run out by the end of the decade unless serious steps are taken to stop wasting water on the ambitious agricultural projects, he added.

Abdul-Latif al-Muqaren, a water official from the Riyadh-based GCC secretariat, urged GCC states to spend more on water and agricultural research saying it accounted for one percent of total budget spending on farming.
Water remains heavily subsidised in the Gulf, though many states have raised prices in recent years.
The region depends on scarce rainfall, non-renewable underground water and desalination to boost water supplies for a population growing between three to four percent a year.
The conference and a water exhibition, a bi-annual event was attended by Arab, GCC and Western experts on water technology.
Israel, which has trade links with Muscat, did not attend the exhibition, apparently responding to objections from Gulf Arab states, especially Saudi Arabia.
The Jewish state has said it had received an invitation to the Oman event.
Oman in August opened a commercial interest office in Tel Aviv, making the energy-rich sultanate the first Gulf Arab state with economic representation in Israel.
Oman and Qatar have forged ahead of other Gulf states in establishing economic ties with Israel after the Jewish state signed a peace deal with the Palestine Liberation Organisation in 1993.
